north_star.one_sentence_pitch: Ben Skywalker, three years after Fate of the Jedi and quietly hungry for meaningful work, is pulled into a post-war conspiracy around a duplicated wartime shipment manifest his cousin Jacen Solo personally encrypted before his death — and forced to discover that the GAG-era lessons Jacen left inside him still work, even when saving lives requires using them.
north_star.reader_promise: A post-Fate of the Jedi Legends conspiracy thriller written to commercial-novel quality: murder, clue, prison break, uneasy partnership, archive attack, respected charity with a hidden inner ring, offworld Force-site climax, rescue, duel, and a morally dangerous ending. Ben as protagonist; Talon Veyr as wounded rogue partner; Aevyn Soris as Ben's true mirror — the other student of Jacen, the side project who lived in the gaps.
north_star.emotional_core: Can Ben face what Jacen left inside him without becoming another unfinished piece of Jacen's legacy?
north_star.author_intent: Reader pleasure before theme. The reader should finish remembering a tense Star Wars adventure with Ben Skywalker, a great rogue partner, a creepy Jacen legacy mystery, an offworld Force-site climax, and a morally dangerous ending. Only afterward should the deeper themes — restraint can cost lives, Jacen's crisis logic can save lives, forbidden knowledge may be necessary to heal or protect people — fully settle in. Ben's danger is not that he wants to become Jacen; it is that he wants to make sure Jacen was not meaningless.

decisions.decision: ~47 ABY, roughly three years after the close of Fate of the Jedi. Coruscant anchors Acts 1-2; Iresh (remote wind-scoured world) anchors Act 3; coda returns to Coruscant / Shedu Maad.
Conspiracy thriller with Star Wars mythic/Force climax. NOT a galactic-war story; a morally tense postwar investigation into the afterlife of Jacen/Caedus, GAG, and dangerous knowledge.
Standalone-but-series-capable. 38 chapters. Commercial-novel quality of storytelling and prose. Fanfiction, non-commercial.

Dorvan administration in return-to-normalcy mode. Jedi based at Shedu Maad (Hapes). Jagged Fel still Imperial Remnant head of state; Tenel Ka still Queen Mother of Hapes. The Dorvan administration has restored procedure, not trust.

Post-FOTJ Legends continues normally. Crucible (45 ABY) is canon; Luke/Leia/Han are post-Mortis-encounter and effectively retired. Legacy comics did NOT happen. The One Sith on Korriban exist and remain in patient pre-emergence under Darth Krayt.

decisions.topic: Force mechanics — Iresh and the Glasswell
decisions.decision: Iresh preserves impressions of identity, memory, and decision under pressure. It does NOT show the future, reveal truth, or grant prophecy. The Glasswell is a natural site (mirror-lake / sinkhole / pale translucent mineral) Jacen exploited for practical concealment — not a Sith temple, Jedi ruin, or mystical treasure chamber.

Unfinished working holocron assembled during LotF period from Jacen's Force-odyssey notes, Vergerean thought, Lumiya's Sith inheritance, GAG-era observations, and Jacen's private systematization of Recognition, Deepening, and Holding. Part notebook, part training device, part confession, part contingency, part laboratory.

Jedi Order HQ relocated permanently to Shedu Maad (Hapes Cluster) at end of FOTJ (44 ABY). Saba Sebatyne is Grand Master. Luke is senior Master on the Council, stepped back after Crucible. Coruscant Jedi Temple is no longer Order property. Luke can advise but not convene; escalation runs through Saba.

Reader-facing clue vocabulary stays in physical thriller terms: fragment, duplicate manifest, quarantine disguise, archive, Foundation link, Iresh manifest/authorization. Avoid stacking abstract internal-system labels. Avoid 'system' as default GAG metaphor — prefer logistics network, shipment trail, records chain, transfer chain, operation.

Close third, multi-POV. Primary POVs: Ben Skywalker (most chapters), Talon Veyr (selected). Single-chapter POVs: Elya Rane (Ch 1 hook), Sela Dray (Iresh chapters), Tess (PP2 opening, Coda Ch 37), Aevyn (Ch 30 + duel-side flashes). Past tense. POV labels are stable per chapter — see Chapter Outlines v4.0.

Commercial readability beats literary flourish. Cinematic clarity, adventure momentum, lived-in technology, dry humor, mythic Force awe when earned. Do NOT imitate any specific published Star Wars author's prose. Show emotion through behavior, pressure, cost, consequence — not through thesis dialogue or interior philosophizing.

No line should sound wiser, cooler, or more poetic than the character would naturally be. Use humor, irritation, silence, avoidance, practical choices, and physical behavior to show emotion. Keep metaphor light and POV-specific. When a line sounds 'cool,' check whether it sounds like the character.

Every scene packet must include a character_voice_focus note for each POV/major participant — how that character's life experience shapes the scene's dialogue, humor, fear response, and avoidance behavior. Per Planning Bible §0C.

Ben should NOT repeatedly ask himself 'Am I becoming Jacen?' The stronger version is that other characters react to him before he fully admits what they saw. Show buried fear through behavior (covering an old GAG sender code, clocking exits, voice that makes Talon stop joking) before direct reflection.

Ben Skywalker, ~21. Jedi Knight, son of Luke and Mara. Lie believed: that the GAG year and Jacen's training have been categorized away as victim/survivor/symbol. Ghost: served under Jacen/GAG at 14; Jacen killed Mara. Want: solve the murder, stop the conspiracy, understand what Jacen left behind. Need: make his past useful as more than damage without surrendering ownership of himself to Jacen. Arc: positive but morally compromised — ends recognizably heroic, but the warning sign is that his most dangerous choices are also his most defensible ones.

Talon Veyr, 28. Former GAG field agent turned black-channel logistics officer; imprisoned at story start. Lie believed: that being funny will keep the past at a manageable distance. Ghost: Operation Glasshook — disobeyed Tess to save trapped civilians/troops; Tess reassigned him into the logistics/records network that later made him look guilty. Want: stay free, stay alive, avoid being used again. Need: prove he was not only a tool in someone else's machine. Pressure valve and tempo engine; the book's humanizing counterweight to Ben's mythic burden.

Aevyn Soris, 28. Jacen's surviving student; Ben's true mirror. Marginal Force-sensitive politely rejected by Jedi at 14 ('we're not able to offer placement at this time'); joined GAG as a young adult; Jacen found him there as a SIDE PROJECT while Ben was Jacen's primary fourteen-year-old apprentice. Lie believed: that Jacen Solo can be separated from Darth Caedus. Ghost: the corridor moment — Jacen left a Recognition session with Aevyn to walk off with young Ben; the 'later' never came. Want: recover the unfinished holocron and finish the lesson. Need (unmet): to admit he was useful, not chosen. Cold white-blue self-built unstable blade fractures more visibly when Ben uses Jacen-derived logic successfully — visual tell, not exposition.

Colonel Maro Tess, ~49. Former senior GAG operations officer; current Greyline Strategic Services strategist; operational architect for the Vigil; knowing One Sith asset. Talon's former mentor. Calm, normal, practical — terrifying because he treats people as logistics. Surface want: contain exposure, preserve assets, continue the larger operation. Deeper want: prove control is the only morality that survives crisis. NO villain poetry.

Aelia Vandros, late fifties. Executive Director of the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation; public face of the conspiracy. Former Senate staffer and widow from the Second Galactic Civil War. Warm, polished, dangerous because much of what she says is true — she genuinely helps grieving families while privately preserving an ideology that grew from Jacen's wartime logic. Beats Ben SOCIALLY before she is exposed operationally. End-of-book fate: steps down in public disgrace to preserve the Foundation's legitimate charitable work; private moral collapse visible.

Iressa Vossk (renamed from Mira Vossk — avoids Mara collision). Former GAG Manifest Integrity Analyst now at Civitas Archive Systems. Lie believed: that survival made her a coward. Want: keep her job, stay alive, get paid. Need: have one old choice matter. Dies at the GAG archive (Ch 15) actively denying Vara a clean copy and transmitting BOTH the documentary chain AND the identity-shaping revelation about the holocron's purpose. Short arc: old Iressa buried discrepancies; new Iressa preserves one.

Commander Elya Rane, former GAG records/logistics officer. POV of Ch 1 in full through her death. Once quietly removed Ben's name from a wrong approval field when he was 14 — that small human correction is why she contacts Ben specifically. Murdered by Aevyn via Jacen-derived memory pressure / Recognition / Holding. The fragment she preserved survives beyond what Aevyn extracts.

Sela Dray, early thirties. Practical Iresh local liaison who knows weather, paths, chimes, taboo ground. Survives Book 1 (NOT another Iressa-style doomed ally). Tavi Dray (younger relative/apprentice) is her personal stake — pressured/paid by the Foundation into the Glasswell zone. Sela's climax job: save Tavi/locals through local knowledge Ben does NOT have.

Luke Skywalker. Senior Master, stepped back post-Crucible (45 ABY Mortis-adjacent encounter — written through implication, not exposition). Based at Shedu Maad through novel events; communicates with Ben on Coruscant by holo. Three Book 1 conversations: Ch 3 (first holo call), Ch 16 (Midpoint Luke + Saba calls), Ch 20 (second Luke call from apartment after PP2), Ch 36 (in-person coda exchange). Emotionally intelligent — NOT absent, foolish, or conveniently fooled.

Bren Korda, early forties. Old GAG security lieutenant in respectable clothing; Director of Protective Services for the Foundation. Talon knew him during GAG and disliked him. Fate: killed/discarded by Tess as public fall guy at PP2.

Vara Senn, former Lost Tribe apprentice now doing mercenary work. NOT Ben's main mirror. Crude dark-side contrast to Aevyn. Pinch Point 1 archive attack: short ugly lightsaber clash with Ben (Lost Tribe footwork + brief Vestara Khai scar-tissue mention), then takes Iressa hostage when combat doesn't work. Whether Vara returns after the archive is OPEN.

HARD not-in-this-book list: Vestara Khai (mention only), Tahiri Veila (one passing reference allowed if natural — no Caedus mention), Han and Leia (mention only), Allana/Amelia (hidden engine, future danger), Jaina (deliberately excluded — would be using her grief), full Krayt/One Sith reveal (hand glimpsed only), Dorvan brainwashing (future target, not yet compromised).

Larry Brooks Story Engineering as LOOSE architectural overlay (function over percentile precision). 38 chapters total. Four-part Brooks beat map with milestones tagged to specific chapter numbers per Chapter Outlines v4.0.

Elya Rane's discovery of the duplicated Jacen-encrypted manifest and her death at Aevyn's hands, as ONE sustained opening chapter (formerly Chs 1+2). Opens the central mystery: why did one of Jacen's last shipments have two lives?
Ben recovers the damaged fragment from the murder scene and realizes the trail points to Talon Veyr in prison. The case becomes Ben's.

The storm-line prison escape from Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works. Ben breaks cover and rescues Talon during a Cinderline snatch attack; they escape via the sea-wall route. Forced partnership is the door Ben cannot return through.

The Cinderline archive cleanup attack and Iressa's hostage death. Vara/Ben short ugly lightsaber clash, then Vara takes Iressa hostage. Ben refuses a Jacen-shaped coercive move that might save her. Iressa dies denying Vara a clean copy and transmitting the dying package. Restraint can cost lives.

Aftermath of Iressa's death. Iressa's transmission carries the documentary chain AND the identity-shaping revelation (the Vigil intends to use the holocron's Recognition/Deepening/Holding for identity-shaping influence on high-value targets, with Aevyn as Jacen's surviving student). Ben does the right thing first: holo-calls Luke and Saba. Both correct, both too slow. Ben pivots from investigator to active disruptor — going to Iresh themselves.

Three-part compounding pressure within hours: (1) Tess clears the board by killing Korda as public fall-guy and accelerates Iresh because Ben/Talon are involved; (2) Iressa's secondary cache is raided and burned — the documentary case for Saba is unrecoverable, breach point unidentified; (3) Talon is framed for a current Coruscant crime with TESS'S TRADECRAFT FINGERPRINT — Luke's quiet legal cover collapses, and Talon reads accelerated Iresh staging through public freight indicators. Every door except off-grid Iresh closes. Ben and Talon relocate to the Skywalker family apartment as final refuge.

The cache site on Iresh. Ben confirms what Iressa told them at the Midpoint — the holocron's unfinished Recognition/Deepening/Holding work, Aevyn's presence as surviving student, the Vigil's intent. SPP is EMBODIMENT not revelation (revelation lives at Midpoint). The threat becomes inescapable: Aevyn is already cracking the cache; only options are rescue and denial.

decisions.topic: Climax — Ch 31-32 (~82-84%) — RESCUE FIRST, DUEL SECOND
decisions.decision: The Glasswell sequence. Ch 31: Ben uses Jacen-shaped crisis logic to save Tavi, Sela's locals, and others — the ordinary Jedi path fails first; some are grateful, some shaken by how it felt to be moved or commanded. Ch 32: Aevyn turns on Ben; consolidated lightsaber duel across the collapsing Glasswell (formerly Chs 40+41). Two students of Jacen arguing through action over what his lessons mean. Ben wins by refusing to let Jacen own what he does with the lessons.

Ch 33 flood/extraction; Ch 34 Iresh aftermath (Sela/Tavi imperfect reunion); Ch 35 Foundation survives — Aelia steps down, Korda is dead fall guy; Ch 36 'Gone where?' in-person Luke/Ben holocron exchange; Ch 37 Tess survives and retreats deeper into One Sith service (POV); Ch 38 cold white-blue spark in the dark — Aevyn survived.

Hook promise: 'why did one of Jacen's last shipments have two lives?' — paid at Midpoint + Ch 29 SPP. FPP promise: forced Ben/Talon partnership — paid through Act 2-3. PP1 promise: restraint can cost lives — paid at Midpoint pivot. PP2 promise: every door but Iresh is closed — paid at Climax. Long-series seed: Ben preserves dangerous knowledge for defensible reasons; Aevyn presumed dead but secretly survives.

Single oblique mention in Ch 37 (Tess / One Sith hand POV) embedded in Tess's post-Iresh review of unresolved assets. Honors the bible's 'dangerous gray zone: suspected/known by some, publicly deniable, potentially weaponizable' framing.

decisions.topic: Voice reference authors (register samples, not voice templates)
decisions.decision: Anchor as REGISTER SAMPLES for sentence-level rhythm and dialogue density, NOT voice templates — the bible forbids imitating any specific SW author. Picks: (1) Aaron Allston (X-Wing, Betrayal) — tempo, banter, partnership energy, prison/procedural texture → Talon's voice + Ben/Talon dynamic. (2) Timothy Zahn (Thrawn, Outbound Flight) — calm operational antagonist register, controlled interiority → Tess + Ben's POV discipline. (3) Karen Traviss (Republic/Imperial Commando) — institutional/procedural detail handled as character not lecture → GAG manifest investigation register. (4) Tana French (In the Woods, Broken Harbor) — non-SW touchstone for precision-with-buried-wound interiority → Aevyn. Voice-discovery surface should record these in voice.reference_authors with explicit 'register sample, not voice copy' annotation.

Vara DISAPPEARS into the contractor pool after the Ch 14-15 archive cleanup attack — she does not return on-page in Book 1. Rationale: (a) Acts 2-3 antagonist column is already loaded (Aevyn returning, Tess emerging, Korda death, Aelia social arc); (b) Vara's function is 'warning shot,' not mirror — Aevyn is the mirror; pulling Vara back would diffuse him; (c) the book's thematic argument is that the cheap closure is denied (Iressa dies, Vara walks, the system survives). Vara left loose is a Book 2 seed.

QUIET RETIREMENT, no criminal liability. Korda is the dead public fall guy; the Foundation's lawyers buffer Aelia; she steps down 'to preserve the Foundation's legitimate work' (her phrasing, public-facing) in Ch 35. Private moral collapse visible in the coda but unpunished. Rationale: (a) compounds the 'harm persists' thematic argument; (b) Book 1 has no room for legal-procedural denouement chapters; (c) preserves Foundation/Vigil residue that carries forward into the series. The cancer stays in the body politic.

KEEP UNNAMED (bible's stated preference). The hand is structurally a position, not a character — exactly what Book 1 needs. Appears only in Ch 37 (POV: Tess or the hand itself, drafter's choice) as an off-page voice / message / presence. No backstory commitment; no on-screen body. Rationale: a name would require backstory commitment, would invite 'who is this and where do they come from' Book 2 prerequisites before the series identity is fixed, and would lift the One Sith veil too early. 'Full reveal of Darth Krayt / the One Sith — the hand is glimpsed or implied only' is on the non-negotiables list.

IMPLICATION ONLY. One quiet line of texture in Ben's first Ch 3 holo call to Luke — Luke looks tired in a way Ben does not remember, his eyes seem further away even when he is looking directly at Ben, his pauses are longer. Ben notices and does NOT ask. A reader who knows Crucible reads it as Mortis aftermath; a reader who does not reads it as a father aging into something new. Both work. Mortis is never named on-page (per non-negotiables: 'Crucible aftermath is Luke's unspoken texture, not on-page').
